Angola — the existing corpus (af-angola.json) already has ao-lei-administracao-local-15-16 (Lei n.º 15/16, DECONCENTRATED state administration — provinces/municipalities as administrative units of the state, governors appointed) and correctly notes Angola has never held local/autárquicas elections. This round found a SEPARATE, parallel legal track — a genuine DECENTRALIZED 'poder local' (autarquias) framework, textually rich but confirmed still not operationally activated. The two tracks coexist: one operating (deconcentrated), one legislated-but-dormant (decentralized).

reports.title: Lei n.º 15/17 de 8 de Agosto de 2017 — Lei Orgânica do Poder Local
reports.description: Angola's organic law establishing autarquias locais (decentralized local authorities) — genuinely distinct from ao-lei-administracao-local-15-16's deconcentrated state-administration framework. Verified via OCR of the scanned Diário da República I Série N.º 134 (8 August 2017), hosted by FAOLEX. Art. 22 (Princípio da Autonomia Financeira e Patrimonial): "1. Os órgãos autónomos do Poder Local gozam de plena liberdade de decisão e gestão dos recursos financeiros e do seu património nos termos da Constituição e da lei. 2. Os recursos financeiros das Autarquias Locais devem ser proporcionais às atribuições previstas pela Constituição ou por lei... 3. A lei estabelece que uma parte dos recursos financeiros das Autarquias Locais deve ser proveniente de rendimentos e de impostos locais." Art. 30(2) mandates direct election: "A Assembleia da Autarquia é composta por representantes locais, eleitos por sufrágio universal, livre, directo, secreto e periódico." CRITICALLY, Art. 41 (Princípio do Gradualismo e da Transitoriedade) makes actual rollout contingent on further state action, not automatic: "A institucionalização efectiva das Autarquias Locais obedece ao Princípio do Gradualismo" — "consiste na faculdade dos órgãos competentes do Estado determinarem por lei a oportunidade da sua criação." This gradualism clause is the textual root of why, per ao-lei-13-20-regime-financeiro-autarquias's own dropped note below, no operational autarquia has yet been activated.

reports.title: Lei n.º 13/20 de 14 de Maio de 2020 — Regime Financeiro das Autarquias Locais
reports.description: Angola's implementing financial law for autarquias — the 'lei própria' Art. 22(5) of Lei 15/17 deferred to. Verified via OCR of the scanned Diário da República I Série N.º 64 (14 May 2020). Art. 12(1) lists own-source revenue: property/urban-land taxes (Imposto Predial Urbano, Imposto de Sisa, Taxa de Circulação), licence/service fees, and tariffs. Art. 14 gives the concrete transfer formula: "3. Os recursos do Fundo das Autarquias Locais são as receitas provenientes do correspondente a 20% da receita prevista no Orçamento Geral do Estado, resultante da cobrança dos impostos seguintes: a) Imposto sobre o Rendimento do Trabalho por conta própria; b) ...por conta de outrem; c) Imposto Industrial [excluding diamonds/minerals]; d) Imposto sobre as Sucessões e Doações; e) Imposto sobre a Aplicação de Capitais" — 20% of five named central tax lines, based on "a receita líquida observada para aqueles impostos nos últimos três anos" (a 3-year trailing average). Art. 16 creates the Fundo de Equilíbrio das Autarquias Locais (FEAL), administered by the Finance Ministry, with three sub-accounts: Art. 17(2) "Constituem receitas da SEF 50% do valor das receitas definidas no artigo 14.º"; Art. 18(2) SEA gets 30%; Art. 19(2) SSA gets 20% — i.e. a 50/30/20 internal FEAL split. This is a real, specific, quantitative transfer mechanism (Angola's actual term is 'Fundo das Autarquias Locais'/'FEAL', not 'Fundo de Apoio Municipal' as one might expect by analogy to other countries).
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument, implementing Lei n.º 15/17.

reports.title: Plano de Actividades do Sistema Estatístico Nacional para 2026 (PASEN 2026)
reports.description: INE's own 2026 activity plan, naming the African Charter on Statistics directly as a source of its founding principles: "...entre outros expressos nos princípios fundamentais das estatísticas oficiais e nas boas práticas adoptadas pela Comissão das Nações Unidas, em Abril de 1994 e pela Carta Africana de Estatística, que se encontram em parte reafirmados na Lei 3/11 de 14 de Junho, Lei do SEN." Separately names SADC as a statistical-cooperation/obligations partner: "Garantir o cumprimento das obrigações internacionais e regionais de Angola em matéria de estatística (SADC, FMI, ONU, entre outras organizações)", and lists a distinct planned CPI-adjacent product, "IPCH" (Índice de Preços no Consumidor Harmonizado), as a scheduled monthly compilation activity. The document does NOT explicitly state that the IPCH activity IS the SADC Harmonised CPI — these are two adjacent-but-separately-stated facts, not conflated here per this branch's evidence-strict standard. Complements the existing ao-ine-sen2018-report node's SADC-transmission finding with a newer document and the additional African Charter citation.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national-statistics-system activity plan; this edition covers 2026.

dependencies.basis: Lei 13/20's own Art. 1 framing and its FEAL/transfer-formula provisions directly implement the financial-autonomy principle Lei 15/17 Art. 22(5) explicitly deferred to a future 'lei própria' — Lei 13/20 is that law, not merely a related instrument.

_dropped.edge: Any individual Angolan autarquia (Luanda, Benguela, Huambo, Lobito) -> a self-published municipal budget/financial-statement document
_dropped.why: No primary municipal budget document was located for any Angolan municipality. This is consistent with secondary/journalistic evidence (not cited as a primary finding) that autarquia elections — repeatedly promised for 2020/2021, then 2024, then 2025 — had still not been held as of the most recent evidence checked, and a 2024 UNITA opposition bill proposal titled 'Institucionalização Efectiva das Autarquias Locais' (itself unenacted) further corroborates that 'institucionalização efectiva' per Lei 15/17's own Art. 41 gradualism clause has not yet occurred. IMPORTANT CORRECTION for this branch: earlier framing (in this round's own research brief) that Angola's autarquias began operating with 2020/2021 elections does NOT match what was found — the enabling laws (ao-lei-15-17-poder-local, ao-lei-13-20-regime-financeiro-autarquias) are real and richly detailed, but there is no primary evidence of an elected, fiscally-operative autarquia currently existing. Treat as a law-on-the-books finding, not an operational-tier finding. Angola's OGE 2023 Relatório de Fundamentação was searched in full text for 'autarqui' and 'FEAL' — zero occurrences, further confirming non-implementation as of that budget year. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.21, processing Grok's round-2 follow-up): Grok reported 'high confidence' elections still hadn't been held as of Aug 2026, based only on absence-of-evidence reasoning — independently re-checked this round with a direct, current search. CNE's own official site (cne.ao, fetched directly) carries no autarquia content as of August 2026 (current items concern the National Assembly, election-observer rules, and Zambia's election) — extending the OGE-2023 zero-hits finding forward with a second, more recent primary silence. Press reporting on CNE's own FY2026 budget (angola24horas.com, citing CNE's budget document) states the entire 243-billion-kwanza allocation is earmarked for the 2027 general elections, again with no autarquia line item. A March 2026 press-reported statement attributed to the National Assembly presidency ('as autarquias não podem continuar adiadas' — 'autarquias cannot continue to be delayed') further implies continued non-fulfillment, though only as secondhand reporting, not a primary transcript. No single dispositive primary CNE/MAT decree stating outright that elections have not been held, or cancelling/confirming a date, was found — this remains a confirmed-by-absence finding, now with stronger and more recent corroboration than Grok's own reasoning alone, not a fully closed case. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round): CNE's own live site search (cne.ao), queried today for 'autarquia,' returned ZERO results with no explicit 'no results' message -- a fresh, functional (not just static-menu-browsing) negative-evidence data point strengthening the absence case. MAT's site DOES index 'autarquia' content (5 results), but none address election timing/status -- all concern capacity-building/training for the still-appointed administrative system. The previously secondhand-only quote ('as autarquias não podem continuar adiadas,' attributed to Assembly President Adão de Almeida) was traced more precisely to his November 2025 swearing-in ceremony, but a Google site-search of parlamento.ao for the exact quote returned ZERO matches -- it remains absent from any primary Assembly publication, still secondhand (O País/DW) only. NEW ACCESS FAILURE identified this round: Angola's actual official gazette portal, imprensanacional.gov.ao, is completely unreachable (connection timeout, both WebFetch and live browser navigation, both http/https, multiple retries) -- this is likely the single most probable place a dispositive postponement/cancellation decree would live, and it could not be searched at all this round. governo.gov.ao's own site-search feature also errors out on this query (a functional failure, not a zero-results outcome). Flagging imprensanacional.gov.ao as an entirely UNCHECKED potential source due to access failure -- explicitly recommending a future round retry that specific domain from a different network path, since it has not been ruled out, only found unreachable.
